chapter: Paris, Lester Young, drugs, Mississippi and later sessions
title: Hawkins's welcome in Paris and 52nd Street Jazz with 'Epistrophy'
summary: Parisians cheered Hawkins but booed McGhee; in 1946 Collins recorded 52nd Street Jazz with Fats Navarro, Sonny Stitt and Bud Powell.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: But Hawk as I said at this time, it was just tremendous his going back, because he was so well loved, in Europe. He was quite a big man there. And this was his first time back there. So they didn't boo Hawk. Neither did they boo us, but they would boo -- every time Howard McGhee played they would just boo because they just could not accept bebop.
What about the rest of the audience how did they accept it?

They were very responsive, but he -- Panassi Panaci had enough seats there to kind of disrupt things for her, you know, for a while. But this is how fanatical they were about this. And it was kind of nice seeing Kenny because I had recorded with these, I guess they're all stars at that time. When I came out of the army. This was done in '46. This was called 52nd Street jazz, I believe, and this was a original recording of Kenny's tune "Epistrophy." And in the band was Fats Novarro Navarro, Kenny Durham Durham, Ray Abramson, Eddie Dr. Vertegull Divertiville, and Sonny Stiss Stiff, saxophone, and Bud Powell and Al Hall, guitar, and it was quite a good player. I had a nice little solo on that also.
